limitations_and_boundaries: The study primarily uses the 5XFAD mouse model, which may not fully recapitulate human Alzheimer's disease pathology.
DAM identification is based on transcriptional signatures; functional validation of DAM's protective role is limited.
The Trem2 dependency experiments were performed in a specific genetic background; generalizability to other models or human disease requires further study.
The exact mechanisms by which DAM restrict neurodegeneration remain to be elucidated.
The study does not address whether DAM are beneficial at all disease stages or if they become detrimental later.
The selected source chunks do not report a rescue, reconstitution, reversal, or epistasis experiment; that rung of the causal evidence chain remains untested within this extraction scope.

provenance.text_excerpt: Our analysis identiﬁes a monocyte state, represented in cluster V, a perivascular macrophage group in cluster IV (Zeisel et al., 2015), several lymphocytes sub groups (B cells, T cells, natural killer [NK] cells; clusters VI–VIII), granulocytes (IX–X), and a large group of microglia cells (cluster I; Figures 1B and S1B). Surprisingly, our analysis also identiﬁes two small groups of cells, clusters II (4.2%) and III (2.8%), which displayed expression of microglial genes (Cst3 and Hexb) with an additional unique signature of lipid metabolism and phagocytic genes such as Apolipoprotein E (Apoe), lipoprotein lipase (Lpl), and Cystatin F (Cst7)
